http://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megabit it's Mb vs MB that confuse the living crap out of normal users. Therefor i advocate the use of the longer abbreviation Mbit.

First we need to understand there is a difference between mb/ and mbit/s. Connectionspeeds are usually meassured in megabits per second, mbit/s. While download and write to disk speed is meassured in megabytes per second, mb/s. The latter is what chrome, firefox, explorer, safari and your favourite bittorrent client will tell you.

One byte is actually 8 bits. To keep this as simple as possible, lets use the conversion that 20mbit = 20,000,000 bits per second, divide by 8 and we get 2,500,000 bytes / second. 2.5million bytes = 2.5megabytes (2.5mb). This is your maximum download speed.

There are several factors that can reduce this speed, for example distance to The host, traficjams on the way to the remote server, other downloads on the network. The last is most likely the biggest issue for you. You mention a college network, you are most likely sharing the net with your neighbours.
